author: Kotomi-Du
title: PyTorch Detectron2 model-hub tests fail to download weights due to expired TLS certificate on dl.fbaipublicfiles.com
signature: ssl certificate verify failed certificate has expired|External Service

failed_jobs.name: PyTorch Models tests / PyTorch Models tests
failed_jobs.symptom: 'PyTorch Detectron2 Tests' step failed: every parametrized test case raised URLError while downloading model weights.

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregated status check failed because the PyTorch Models tests job it depends on failed.

key_errors: install/tests/model_hub_tests/pytorch/test_detectron2.py::TestDetectron2ConvertModel::test_detectron2_precommit[CPU-COCO-Detection/faster_rcnn_R_50_FPN_1x-none-None-None] FAILED [  5%] (and 17 more parametrized cases, 100% of the Detectron2 suite)

Attempt 2 of 3 failed: <urlopen error [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: certificate has expired (_ssl.c:1018)>
Attempt 3 of 3 failed: <urlopen error [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: certificate has expired (_ssl.c:1018)>
root_cause: All 18 Detectron2 model-hub precommit test cases fail identically at model-weight download time: detectron2's checkpointer calls iopath's PathManager.get_local_path, which falls through to urllib.request.urlretrieve against the external host serving the pretrained checkpoint files (Facebook AI's public model zoo, reached via detectron2's own download helper, not the pip-proxy mirror used for package installs). The TLS handshake fails with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED: certificate has expired, i.e. the externally hosted certificate on the model-weights host has expired server-side - this is outside OpenVINO's or this PR's control and unrelated to the PR's source changes (GPU plugin transformation/oneDNN code, which the Detectron2 suite does not exercise). This exact signature has now recurred 9 times in the last ~12 hours across unrelated PRs, confirming it is an ongoing upstream certificate outage rather than a one-off blip.
reproduction_steps: Not reproducible via this PR's changes. To reproduce the download failure directly: `curl -v https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/detectron2/...` (or whichever exact weights URL config.MODEL.WEIGHTS resolves to for the failing configs) from a machine with up-to-date CA trust and observe the expired-certificate TLS error; or run `python -m pytest install/tests/model_hub_tests/pytorch/test_detectron2.py -k test_detectron2_precommit` locally with network access to the same host.
recommended_actions: No PR-side fix needed; this is an upstream certificate problem on the external model-weights host used by detectron2's checkpoint loader.
Re-run the failed 'PyTorch Detectron2 Tests' step (or the whole job) once the upstream certificate is renewed - automated transient remediation has been requested for this run.

If the outage persists beyond a few hours, consider temporarily skipping/xfailing the Detectron2 precommit suite in CI and notify the model-hub test maintainers to mirror the weights or pin a vetted snapshot.
Escalate to the detectron2/model-zoo host owner (Facebook AI) if the certificate remains expired, since repeated reruns will keep failing until it is renewed.
prevention_strategies: Model-hub tests that download third-party artifacts over HTTPS should use a mirrored/cached copy inside OpenVINO's own infrastructure (or the pip-proxy) rather than depending directly on an externally hosted, unmonitored TLS endpoint whose certificate lifecycle is outside the project's control. Add a lightweight pre-flight certificate/reachability check with a clear, distinct failure message so a cert-expiry outage is visually distinguishable from a genuine model-conversion regression at a glance.
historical_context: Identical signature (2641a2995515ec82) recorded 8 prior times in roughly the same 12-hour window (first seen 2026-11-12T01:09:15Z, most recently 2026-11-12T09:49:41Z) across PRs #39753, #38204 (this PR, previously), #39752, #39201 and #39727, all with the same URLError: certificate has expired root cause. Automated remediation and a rerun-pattern proposal were already issued for earlier occurrences; the upstream certificate has not yet been renewed.
